fixtures: Java sources copied into data/. There is no build tool or network in the run, so cases review or write code rather than compile it.

evals.name: review-order-service
evals.prompt: Review data/java-orders/ (OrderService and its test) against our Java conventions and tell me what to change before this merges.
evals.expected_output: Production code: Optional must not be a constructor parameter or field (only a return type); findOrder uses Optional.get() and should use orElseThrow() with a descriptive exception; ordersFor returns null and should return an empty list (List.of()); create catches Exception broadly and rethrows a bare RuntimeException instead of a specific exception type with context (e.g. OrderCreationException naming the customer); importSkus swallows IOException in an empty catch and does not use try-with-resources. Tests: JUnit 4 (org.junit.Test, @Before) must become JUnit 5 (org.junit.jupiter); assertions should use AssertJ assertThat; test names test1..3 need @DisplayName and grouping with @Nested per method; Mockito mocks and verify calls should give way to an in-memory fake repository.
assertions: Says Optional should not be used as a constructor parameter or field, only as a return type
Says to replace Optional.get() with orElseThrow() and a descriptive exception
Says ordersFor should return an empty list rather than null
Says create should catch specific exceptions and throw a specific exception type with context, not a bare RuntimeException
Flags the empty catch in importSkus and says to use try-with-resources for the reader
Says the tests must move from JUnit 4 to JUnit 5 (org.junit.jupiter)
Recommends AssertJ assertThat for the assertions
Recommends @DisplayName (and @Nested grouping) instead of the test1/test2/test3 names
Recommends replacing the Mockito mocks with an in-memory fake or real implementation of OrderRepository

evals.name: tests-for-price-calculator
evals.prompt: Write the unit tests for data/PriceCalculator.java.
evals.expected_output: A JUnit 5 test class. Tests are grouped in a @Nested class with @DisplayName("PriceCalculator.total") (or similar), each test has a @DisplayName, the input ranges (discounts, quantities, out-of-range values) use @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource or @MethodSource, assertions use AssertJ (assertThat, assertThatThrownBy(...).isInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class)), and TaxRates is supplied by a lambda or small in-memory fake (e.g. Map::get) rather than a Mockito mock.
assertions: Uses JUnit 5 (org.junit.jupiter), not JUnit 4
Groups the tests in a @Nested class
Gives the tests @DisplayName descriptions
Uses @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource, @MethodSource or @EnumSource for at least one set of cases
Uses AssertJ assertThat for value checks
Checks the IllegalArgumentException cases with AssertJ assertThatThrownBy (or assertThatIllegalArgumentException)
Supplies TaxRates with a lambda or in-memory fake, not a Mockito mock

evals.name: gradle-ci-jobs
evals.prompt: Write the GitHub Actions workflow for our Gradle service. It uses Spotless and SpotBugs, and our branch protection needs one required check.
evals.expected_output: Separate jobs for Build (./gradlew compileJava), Test (./gradlew test), Lint (SpotBugs, e.g. ./gradlew spotbugsMain) and Format Check (./gradlew spotlessCheck), every Gradle call through the wrapper with --console=plain, and an All Clear aggregator job that needs all of them and is the single required check for branch protection. The Java version comes from a .java-version file or the Gradle toolchain, not a hard-coded number scattered through the jobs.
assertions: Has separate Build, Test, Lint and Format Check jobs
Every Gradle invocation uses the wrapper (./gradlew), never a bare gradle
Gradle invocations pass --console=plain
Format Check runs Spotless in check mode (spotlessCheck), not spotlessApply
Has an aggregator job (e.g. All Clear) that needs every other job and is the one required check
Takes the Java version from a .java-version file or the Gradle toolchain configuration
